stories.title: Man Named 'Service' Cleans Up NYC Dumping Site on His Own Initiative
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A Queens man named Joshua Service spotted an illegal dumping site while riding the rails and decided to do something about it instead of just scrolling past. He rolled up his sleeves and cleared the mess himself, turning an eyesore back into a clean public space. No committee, no funding request, just one neighbor deciding the street deserved better. It's a nice reminder that a cleaner block can start with a single person who stops and acts. Sometimes the simplest good deeds are the ones that stick with you.
stories.why_good: A real person took real, voluntary action to improve a shared public space, with no political angle and no catch.

stories.title: Numbers of Endangered and Sacred River Dolphin Grow by 6 After Successful Breeding Season
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Six new calves were born this season to the rare Irrawaddy dolphins that live in the Mekong River and are considered sacred by local communities in Cambodia. These gentle river dolphins are critically endangered, so every new calf is a big deal for the species' survival. Conservationists who have been protecting the river and working with fishing communities say this is one of the strongest breeding seasons in years. It's a hopeful sign that patient, local conservation work is paying off for one of the world's rarest dolphins.
stories.why_good: A real, counted increase in a critically endangered animal population thanks to successful on-the-ground conservation work.

stories.title: Stunning New Opera House Opens With a Gravity-Defying Grand Staircase
stories.label: world
stories.summary: Shanghai has just opened a brand-new opera house, and it's already turning heads around the world. The building sits right on the banks of the Huangpu River and features a jaw-dropping staircase that seems to float in midair. It's the kind of grand, hopeful public project that brings people together to enjoy art and music in a beautiful new space. Cities investing in culture and design like this are a lovely reminder of what communities can build when they aim high.
stories.why_good: A real, completed public building that celebrates art and architecture, with no suffering or controversy attached.
